caps.name: predict_class
caps.description: Classify a 30-dimensional breast-tumor feature vector (sklearn load_breast_cancer schema) into a binary diagnosis: 0 = malignant, 1 = benign.

features.description: 30-dim float feature vector in load_breast_cancer order (mean radius ... worst fractal dimension)

caps.failure_boundary: Fails or returns unreliable output if features is not exactly 30 numeric values, if values are on a different scale than training data, or if the frozen model.json weights are missing/corrupted (SHA256 mismatch). No input validation or schema coercion is performed by the function itself.

caps.name: predict_probability
caps.description: Return calibrated class probabilities for a 30-dim feature vector as a mapping of class label to probability.

features.description: 30-dim float feature vector in load_breast_cancer schema order

caps.failure_boundary: Same input constraints as predict: requires exactly 30 numeric features at training scale. Probabilities are only meaningful for in-distribution inputs; out-of-distribution vectors may yield overconfident scores. Fails if model weights are unavailable.

caps.name: explain_feature_importance
caps.description: Report the top-k most important features ranked by XGBoost gain importance, enabling global model interpretability.

top_k.description: number of top features to return

output_schema.description: Ordered list of top-k feature importance entries (feature name/index with gain score), descending by importance

caps.failure_boundary: top_k must be a positive integer; values above 30 exceed the feature count. Returns global (dataset-level) importance only — it does not explain any individual prediction. Fails if model weights are unavailable.

caps.name: list_classes
caps.description: Return the class labels the model was trained on, allowing callers to map numeric outputs to semantic labels.
caps.failure_boundary: Requires the model to be loaded; returns static metadata and does not validate any input. Fails if model weights are unavailable.
